episodes.211301: A mesoscale convective system moved east-southeastward through central Mississippi into southwestern Alabama late on April 24. Although it mostly missed Central Alabama, it clipped southern Sumter County, resulting in a few downed trees.
episodes.211649: A thunderstorm moving offshore produced a strong wind gust at the Melbourne Airport.
episodes.211772: Numerous hail-producing thunderstorms (supercells) developed along a slow-moving frontal boundary across south-central into southeast Oklahoma from the early afternoon into evening of the 24th.
episodes.211773: Another widespread thunderstorm and severe weather period impacted the southern one-half of Oklahoma and adjacent north Texas on the evening of the 25th. This event included several supercell thunderstorms across this area, including a cyclic tornadic supercell that moved in areas south of Wichita Falls, Texas into Archer and Clay Counties. Several other (generally brief) tornadoes occurred with storms across south-central and southeastern Oklahoma, though signal of residual inhibition and numerous storm interactions on the cool side of a quasi-stationary boundary generally limited low-level mesocyclone organization and longevity. Large hail and sporadic wind damage also occurred with storms across the region.

episodes.211868: On the evening of 4/25, a few severe storms developed in north central Kansas before gradually weakening towards the southeast in the late evening hours. Storms produced hail to quarter size and wind gusts around 60 mph.
episodes.211941: Strong thunderstorms developed into northeastern Oklahoma during the late evening of the 23rd, as a cold front moved into the area. The strongest thunderstorms produced hail up to nickel size. ||Another round of thunderstorms developed along the cold front over east central and southeastern Oklahoma during the afternoon of the 24th. The strongest thunderstorms produced large hail up to golf ball size and a tornado.
episodes.211943: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed across eastern Oklahoma during the early evening of the 25th, north of a warm front near the Red River, as an upper level disturbance approached the region from the west. The atmosphere north of the warm front across eastern Oklahoma became moderately unstable during the afternoon and early evening, and the deep-layer wind shear was strong with the approach of the upper level disturbance. Some of the thunderstorms were able to develop into supercells due to the favorable combination of instability and wind shear. Large hail up to tennis ball size occurred with the strongest thunderstorms, as well as isolated damaging wind.
episodes.211971: From April 24 to April 27, daily thunderstorms developed during the late afternoon and evening, triggered by a dryline and a meandering frontal boundary. These long-lasting supercells were fueled by a highly unstable and sheared environment, resulting in several tornadoes, damaging winds, and very large hail. Two fatalities occurred on April 25th.
episodes.212592: Scattered storms developed along a stationary front across south-central Virginia on April 25 as a weak surface low moved into the area. An isolate severe storm developed across southeast Virginia on the leading edge of the storms.
episodes.212614: Scattered thunderstorms moved through central Louisiana with a cold front. An isolated severe storm occurred.
episodes.212680: In the afternoon of 4/25, two strong storms both producing severe hail with one producing 2.5 hail. Some severe wind gusts were also reported. A cold front bisected the area and interacted with a shortwave that produced organized convection with low level moisture and deep-layer shear. The shear CAPE available generated numerous reports of severe winds while the steep lapse rates aided in generating severe wind gusts.
episodes.212684: Multiple organized QLCSs push across central Mississippi and produced damaging wind gusts and several tornadoes.
episodes.212845: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and through the evening on April 24th as a cold front advanced from Southeast Oklahoma into the Ark-La-Tex. Intersecting this front was an outflow boundary, which moved west southwest out of Arkansas toward Northeast Texas and Northern Louisiana. This same boundary was slow in advancing and showed signs of stalling across Southeast Oklahoma just ahead of the cold front. Low-level shear in this area was sufficient to support strong updrafts with 0-1 km storm-relative helicity (SRH) over 100 m2/s2. The air mass was very moist and unstable with deep-layer shear around 50 knots, further aiding storm longevity. As a result, a few severe thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts across parts of Hempstead County in Southwest Arkansas.
episodes.212920: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and through the evening on April 24th as a cold front advanced from Southeast Oklahoma into the Ark-La-Tex. Intersecting this front was an outflow boundary, which moved west southwest out of Arkansas toward Northeast Texas and Northern Louisiana. This same boundary was slow in advancing and showed signs of stalling across Southeast Oklahoma just ahead of the cold front. Low-level shear in this area was sufficient to support strong updrafts with 0-1 km storm-relative helicity (SRH) over 100 m2/s2. The air mass was very moist and unstable with deep-layer shear around 50 knots, further aiding storm longevity. As a result, numerous severe thunderstorms developed across Northeast Texas during the evening with reports of widespread damaging wind gusts along with a handful of large hail reports.
episodes.213018: During the afternoon and evening of April 25th, 2026, thunderstorms advancing into eastern Nebraska produced isolated pockets of large hail. This convection was driven by a cold front sweeping through the area. Ahead of the boundary, dewpoints rose into the mid-50s, supporting modest elevated instability (MUCAPE up to 1000 J/kg) alongside adequate deep-layer bulk shear. The first hail report was received around 4:56 PM CST near Seward, NE. Additional reports of hail up to 1.5 inches in diameter were received in Beatrice, NE, while a 1.75-inch hailstone was reported near Elk Creek, NE. Convective activity gradually decayed into the evening hours.
episodes.213039: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and evening hours of April 25th. Several reports of large hail were received with the largest being golf ball sized.
episodes.213197: Thunderstorms developed across southeast Oklahoma during the late afternoon of April 24th, then congealed into a partially organized cluster of storms as they moved southeast across the ArkLaTex region during the evening. The storms continued to strengthen and evolved into a more organized mesoscale convective system within northwest flow aloft as they approached the local area. This MCS moved across southeast Louisiana late that night into the early morning hours of April 25th, producing scattered damaging wind gusts. Several reports of thunderstorm wind damage occurred across the area, mainly from downed trees and large limbs.
episodes.213199: Thunderstorms developed across southeast Oklahoma during the late afternoon of April 24th, then congealed into a partially organized cluster of storms as they moved southeast across the ArkLaTex region during the evening. The storms continued to strengthen and evolved into a more organized mesoscale convective system within northwest flow aloft as they approached the local area. The MCS moved across coastal Mississippi on the early morning hours of April 25th, producing a couple of tornadoes along with areas of flash flooding.
episodes.213216: Strong thunderstorms moved over the marine area and produced gusty winds.

An EF-1 tornado with peak winds of 95 mph touched down just north of the intersection of Ohio Ave. and Polk St. in Gulfport. The tornado quickly tracked to the south causing sporadic tree damage that consisted primarily of large tree limbs being blown off of trees as tracked southward between Wisconsin Ave. and West Railroad Ave. The tornado continued south-southeast across US Hwy 49 with visible damage observed to commercial businesses in this area. Large branches and snapped trees were observed between 34th St. and 28th St. At the intersection of 28th St. and 22nd Ave. two metal buildings had their garage doors blown out as the tornado continued south-southeast. At the intersection of Pass Road and 22nd Ave. a large hardwood tree was completely uprooted. The tornado then crossed Pass Road and produced additional tree damage in the form of large branches and a few snapped trees. The snapped trees were either dead and diseased, so the windspeed was lowered to 90 mph to account for this. As the tornado crossed the railroad track, minor damage to a home in the form of a few removed shingles was observed on 3rd St. The tornado then moved offshore near the intersection of Beach Blvd. and Pratt Ave.

An EF-1 tornado with peak winds of 90 mph touched down at 30th Street and Brookwood Ave. where large branches were down on several trees. Similar damage occurred as the tornado tracked to the southeast across Pass Road and 28th Street. The tornado continued to the southeast and reached peak intensity of 90 mph near the intersection of 5th Avenue and 25th Street where a few trees were snapped. One hardwood tree was hollow inside and the other snap was very high. Numerous large branches were also removed from several trees near this intersection. The tornado then continued to the southeast crossing Gulf Avenue near 24th Street producing sporadic tree damage. The tornado then crossed the railroad just west of Hewes St. where additional large branches were removed from several trees all the way to Beach Blvd. Numerous trees were observed to have lost large branches between Roberts Ave. and Centennial Plaza on Beach Blvd.
